source: design-spec-parity-fixtures-4c.md v4 D5 (amendments A1-A7); expected outcomes written by the design's author from REM-PARITY §3.4, §7.1-7.2, §9.1 and §14 before any executor existed, not generated from the reference
portable_input: Each positive and portable negative case gives an image, its committed prefix as §7.1 filemark-map entries, and W and T derived from that prefix by §7.2. A reference adapter turns the prefix into the reference's off-tape commit records; the records are not part of the vector (Appendix B.12). A case's prefix mutation is applied to the image's true committed prefix; the tape bytes are the image's, unchanged.

cases.prefix: the image's committed prefix: files 0-2, blocks [1, 4, 7]
cases.append: one further Object of 2 blocks, committed by finish_object, then a barrier

cases.prefix: the image's committed prefix: files 0-3, blocks [1, 4, 7, 2]
cases.append: one further Object of 2 blocks; the epoch [4, 8) is then complete and its sidecar is written
cases.informative: sidecar_equals_uninterrupted compares the resumed sidecar's bytes with those of the same three Objects written in one session with no interruption; §14 step 3 rebuilds the open epoch's parity and per-block CRCs from the committed data, and §9 defines a sidecar from its epoch's data and metadata only. If the text lets any sidecar byte depend on the session, this becomes a disagreement settled by citation

cases.prefix_mutation: file 1 (the Object) records block_count 3, so T = 3, while the sidecar still protects [0, 4), so W = 4
the prefix is files 0-1 only (the sidecar is not committed), so W = 0 and T = 4 = S x k
file 3 (the final Object) records first_parity_data_ordinal 1, so it ends at 3 while T = 4 (file 1 ends at 4)
cases.informative: §14 step 2 names ResumeAppend; the mutated prefix also breaks §7.2's dense, contiguous first-ordinals, and the text does not order the two checks, so the error name is informative

cases.prefix_mutation: file 3 records block_count 3, so T = 7 and the open epoch is [4, 7); on tape file 3 has 2 blocks, so re-reading ordinal 6 at LBA 17 meets the filemark
cases.informative: §14 step 3 says a boundary read where data is expected is fatal but names no error; the reference's error is recorded, not pinned

cases.prefix_mutation: the prefix is files 0-3 (Bootstrap, the 8-block Object, both sidecars) with the second sidecar's range recorded as [5, 8) instead of [4, 8)
the prefix is files 0-3 with the second sidecar's epoch_id recorded as 2 instead of 1

cases.statement: When a record the Resumer relies on is missing, or the records' claims conflict, or their combination is incomplete or ambiguous, resume fails as ResumeAppend before positioning or writing. The commit record's format is implementation-defined (§3.4), so this is not a portable vector; the reference covers it at its journal-replay layer, which the vector set names.
